business_problem: Caterpillar's finance organization relied on decades-old forecasting processes, hundreds of data sources and countless spreadsheets, leaving teams with limited time for strategic insight and making it difficult to improve forecast accuracy and scenario planning.
solution_summary: Caterpillar's Global Finance Services Division worked with EY to prove how AI- and ML-enabled forecasting could replace labor-intensive financial planning. EY began with a proof of concept that used a shadow copy of Caterpillar data plus selected external sources to build modeling tools and demonstrate better speed, accuracy and scenario analysis without disrupting live operations. The architecture combined EY Data Fabric and EY Intelligent Forecasting and Scenario Modeling with newly developed statistical models, scenario-planning workflows and a custom user interface. The new interface created a global repository for critical planning data and allowed finance teams to run more scenarios, inspect model outputs and override predictions when fresh information arrived. After the proof of concept, the team piloted the solution alongside Caterpillar's current process in one business unit, then used the results to expand advanced analytics capabilities for future finance forecasting work.

data_flow: Caterpillar finance data and selected external sources were copied into an EY modeling environment, where Data Fabric and Intelligent Forecasting and Scenario Modeling supported statistical forecast generation. Results flowed into a custom interface and scenario-planning process so teams could compare outcomes, apply overrides and reuse a central planning-data repository.
business_outcome: Caterpillar established a practical AI-driven forecasting foundation that improved the speed and flexibility of finance planning, created a reusable scenario process and gave the finance organization a scalable method for expanding analytics-based forecasting into additional business areas.
